mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 3.5% over two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of corporate cash flows, which drives negative S&P 500 forward 20-day returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 posts positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the effect reverses during a recession.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincident with a housing starts (HOUST) drop of more than 10% in the prior quarter indicates weakening consumer and housing demand, which depresses corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 achieves positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the relationship inverts during a supply shock.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in the unemployment rate below 3.5% for three consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately reducing profit margins and producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 posts positive 20-day returns in more than 55% of triggered episodes, or the effect is absent during periods of high inflation.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) of more than 1% for four consecutive months signals a broad-based supply-side downturn, which reduces corporate revenues and earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 achieves positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the effect is absent during a demand-driven expansion.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in payrolls (PAYEMS) of more than 200,000 and a decline in unemployment rate (UNRATE) of more than 0.3 percentage points in the same month signals an overheating labor market, which increases wage inflation and cost pressures, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 posts positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of triggered months, or the effect reverses during periods of falling inflation.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp one-month increase in the federal funds rate of more than 0.75 percentage points signals an aggressive tightening stance, which rapidly elevates borrowing costs and reduces capital expenditure, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
regime_hint: immediate reaction window after rate hike
failure_condition: S&P 500 posts positive 5-day returns in more than 70% of triggered instances, or the effect is not statistically significant at p < 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous monthly decline of more than 1% in both real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) indicates a synchronized deterioration in key demand drivers, which reduces corporate sales and earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 < previous month - 1% AND HOUST < previous month - 1%
failure_condition: S&P 500 achieves positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of triggered months, or the effect is not robust during periods of strong export demand.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly inflation rate (CPIAUCSL) above 6% for six consecutive months in the context of stable or rising federal funds rates signals that monetary policy is behind the inflation curve, which erodes real corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL > 6% for six consecutive months AND FEDFUNDS not falling over the period
failure_condition: S&P 500 posts positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the effect disappears if inflation expectations fall sharply.
